newsitem.title: INDIA: Schlumberger sets up Indian subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: Schlumberger sets up Indian subsidiary.

text.p: Global engineering services company Schlumberger Ltd said Wednesday it had set up an Indian subsidiary with an eye on the domestic banking and telecommunication industries.
Schlumberger Measurement and Systems India Ltd, with an initial investment of $10 million, will be headquartered in New Delhi, officials said.
Dugald Euan Baird, the subsidiary's chief executive, told a news conference that the Indian market offered tremendous growth potential for Schlumberger's products.

"We believe that electronic transaction products have a tremendous market potential in India," Baird said. "There will be over two billion smart cards in circulation by the year 2000. A sizeable portion of that will be in India."
Liberalisation of the Indian economy offered more business opportunities for the company, he said.
"The strength of India is that it has a proper consultative democratic process which means changes take place rather slowly but they take place surely," Baird said.
New York-based Schlumberger, a worldwide group with a big presence in Europe, has interests in engineering and services linked to electronic instruments, oil exploration and telecommunications.
